item.name: TD engineering blog scaffolded and live
item.contract: TrebuchetDynamics has a publicly reachable engineering blog with a working Atom/RSS feed, an /about page that names the org and the methodology, and a deploy pipeline so a markdown commit becomes a published post without manual intervention. Hosting choice is owner's call (Astro/Hugo/Eleventy + Cloudflare/Vercel/GitHub Pages); the row is done when a stranger can subscribe to a feed and read one published post.
item.degraded_mode: Without a publication outlet, every loop commit is invisible in the reputation market; the strategy described in success-plan.md cannot start.
ready_when: Hosting choice and blog framework are decided (operator decision; not loop-driven).
A subdomain or path on an existing TD-controlled domain is available.
not_ready_when: The blog is private, password-protected, or behind authentication.
There is no Atom/RSS feed at a stable URL.
The first post is empty or placeholder text rather than the writeup #1 draft or a real introduction.
acceptance: Blog is reachable at a public URL with at least one real (non-placeholder) post.
An Atom or RSS feed exists at a stable, discoverable URL.
Publishing a new post is a markdown-commit-and-merge operation; no console click-through required.
An /about page exists that names TrebuchetDynamics and points at gormes-agent + agentic-porting-kit.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-13: scaffolded the TrebuchetDynamics Engineering Blog under webpages/blog as a static Astro site at https://engineering.trebuchetdynamics.com/ with a discoverable RSS feed at /feed.xml, an /about page naming TrebuchetDynamics, gormes-agent, and the planned agentic-porting-kit, plus one real starter post about the autonomous Hermes-porting loop. Added a Cloudflare Pages deploy workflow so a markdown commit merged to main builds and deploys the blog without console click-through. DNS attachment remains operator-owned through the workflow's Cloudflare secrets. Evidence: cd webpages/blog && npm run test.
done_signal: Public blog URL + feed URL recorded in success-plan.md and README.md.

item.name: TD social presence connected to blog feed
item.contract: A TrebuchetDynamics-named account on at least one public social platform (Twitter/X or Bluesky) exists, follows the engineering blog feed, and has an automation that announces new posts within 1 hour of publication. The platform choice is owner's call; the row is done when a new blog post produces a public social post automatically.
item.degraded_mode: Without distribution, even good writeups die without an audience; this row creates the minimum viable distribution channel.
ready_when: TD blog (8.A row 1) is live and emitting a feed.
Operator has chosen a social platform and created the account.
not_ready_when: Posts are announced manually each time.
Automation depends on a paid-per-post service when free options exist.
blocked_by: TD engineering blog scaffolded and live
acceptance: A test post on the blog produces a corresponding public social post within 1 hour.
The automation is reproducible (scripted, not click-configured).
item.no_test_required: Documentation/research/planning row — automated tests not applicable
done_signal: Social account URL + automation method recorded in success-plan.md.

item.name: README rewrite to methodology-first positioning
item.contract: README.md leads with the autonomous-porting methodology and the sharp v1.0 differentiator (in <50 words), with Hermes appearing as the parity oracle in paragraph 2 — not as the lede. Existing operator-facing sections (install, quick start, status) are preserved; only the framing changes. The README explicitly links to success-plan.md and the agentic-porting-kit repo (or a placeholder section if that kit has not yet been extracted).
item.degraded_mode: Without the rewrite, the public face of the repo positions Gormes as "Hermes in Go" — a clone framing that gives reputation credit to Hermes, not TrebuchetDynamics.
ready_when: docs/content/building-gormes/strategy/v1-differentiator.md is ratified and contains the <50-word differentiator paragraph.
docs/content/building-gormes/strategy/success-plan.md contains the North Star wording and 30-day README action item.
not_ready_when: The differentiator is still 'TBD' or undecided.
Install/quick-start sections are deleted or broken in the rewrite.
The new README still calls Gormes 'a Go port of Hermes' as the lede.
acceptance: TestREADMEStartsWithMethodology asserts the first paragraph mentions the autonomous-porting methodology and does not contain the phrase "Go port".
TestREADMEMentionsDifferentiator asserts the differentiator string from success-plan.md appears within the first 50 words.
TestREADMEPreservesOperatorSections asserts install, quick-start, and status sections still exist with their current commands intact.
TestREADMELinksStrategyDoc asserts a link to success-plan.md is present in the body.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-08: bounded all-topic weakness sweep covered CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public surfaces, and release/operator flows. Planned rows were 33, below the 90-row cap. The sweep found this P1 docs/public row was highest-priority and now unblocked by the ratified v1 differentiator, but its test command still pointed at removed internal/repodocs. Planner pass corrected the row to internal/repoctl README contract tests, then TDD rewrote README.md to lead with the autonomous-porting methodology, state the 30-skill single-binary differentiator within the first 50 words, preserve install/first-run/status commands, link success-plan.md and v1-differentiator.md, and keep Hermes-Agent as attribution/parity oracle rather than the lede.
done_signal: README.md leads with methodology, differentiator stated in <50 words, install/quick-start preserved; assertion tests pass.

item.name: README release and benchmark metadata sync
item.contract: README.md and public benchmark mirrors stay synchronized with the current release metadata and freshly measured optimized Linux binary: the README latest-release stanza, development-head wording, release-summary sentence, benchmark size, and benchmark date are derived from version/release metadata plus benchmarks.json, while repoctl benchmark recording updates every checked-in public benchmark mirror from one source of truth.
item.degraded_mode: If release or benchmark metadata drifts, public trust surfaces can advertise an old release, stale size evidence, or a >30 MB benchmark even after the release pipeline and current optimized build satisfy the v1 size contract.
ready_when: The latest public GitHub release is known from local release metadata or gh release evidence.
A trusted optimized local binary can be built with CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" for benchmark recording.
Existing README methodology and differentiator tests remain green.
not_ready_when: The slice invents release versions or benchmark numbers instead of deriving them from checked-in release/benchmark data and a local optimized build.
The README's fixed v1 differentiator claim is rewritten from the measured current benchmark rather than preserving the ratified 30 MB promise.
Benchmark recording updates only the root file while docs or landing mirrors remain stale.
acceptance: TestUpdateReadmeSyncsReleaseAndBenchmarkMetadata fails while README.md still names v0.1.05 and stale 2026-05-05 benchmark data, then passes after repoctl readme update derives v0.2.0, the release URL, benchmark size, and last_measured date.

TestRecordBenchmarkCopiesBenchmarksToPublicMirrors proves repoctl benchmark record writes identical benchmark JSON to benchmarks.json, docs/data/benchmarks.json, webpages/docs/data/benchmarks.json, webpages/landing/src/data/benchmarks.json, and webpages/landing/legacy/go-renderer/internal/site/data/benchmarks.json.
A fresh optimized Linux build is recorded into benchmarks.json and mirrors, showing the current size evidence below the 30 MB release gate without overwriting the ratified differentiator text.
README release and benchmark prose names the current public release v0.2.0 and current benchmark date/size.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-09: bounded all-topic weakness sweep refreshed Hermes to f1f42a7b9 and Honcho to e659b6b, then checked CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public surfaces, and release/operator flows. Runtime parity drift gates were green or row-backed, planned rows were 13 below the 90-row cap, and higher-priority TD publication rows remained operator-blocked while the broad release parent stayed non-selectable. The unblocked public-surface weakness was stale README and benchmark metadata: GitHub release evidence shows v0.2.0 is latest, release.json already says v0.2.0, and a fresh optimized linux/amd64 build measured below the 30 MB release gate while README still pointed at v0.1.05 and stale 2026-05-05 ~39.1 MB benchmark data. TDD taught repoctl to sync release and benchmark metadata into README, normalize the seven-target benchmark platform matrix, and copy benchmark JSON into docs plus landing mirrors.
done_signal: README, benchmark root data, docs mirrors, landing mirrors, repoctl fixtures, and progress evidence agree on the current release and measured optimized binary size.

implementation: internal/repoctl/bench.go now normalizes the supported release platform matrix and writes identical benchmark JSON to root, docs/data, webpages/docs/data, landing source data, and legacy landing renderer data.

README.md now names v0.2.0 as the latest public release and reports the current benchmark mirror date/size.

item.name: Engineering writeup #1: autonomous Hermes-porting loop
item.contract: A 1500–2500 word engineering writeup published on the TD blog explaining how the autonomous loop ships 1–2 Hermes-parity features per hour with TDD discipline. Includes: an architecture diagram of the loop, a real diff walkthrough of 3+ recent loop-shipped commits (e.g., Telegram thread fallback, browser cleanup, skill validator), the cost-per-feature numbers, and the validation-gate flow. Writes for a reader who has not seen Gormes before.
item.degraded_mode: Without writeup #1, the methodology is invisible to anyone outside the repo; the autonomous loop is a curiosity, not a credential.
ready_when: TD blog (8.A row 1) is live.
Loop $/iteration cost telemetry (8.F) has at least one week of data.
Operator has decided the publication date and platform (HN/Lobsters/Reddit).
not_ready_when: Cost numbers are estimated rather than measured.
The diff walkthrough cherry-picks a single perfect commit; readers see only good outcomes and not honest tradeoffs.
The post is published without operator review of voice and tone.
blocked_by: TD engineering blog scaffolded and live
Loop $/iteration cost metric in status file
unblocks: Engineering writeup #3: Gormes vs Hermes-Python benchmarks
acceptance: Post is published at a public URL with the TD blog feed; a stranger can read it without auth.
Post contains a loop architecture diagram (image or ASCII).
Post walks through 3+ real diff examples with PR/commit links.
Post includes real cost-per-feature numbers from 8.F telemetry.
Post has been submitted to HN/Lobsters at least once (success metric is the submission, not front-page placement).
item.note: Source: success-plan.md 30-day action sprint item #3. Loop can draft structural sections and assemble diff walkthroughs from git log + commit ranges; final voice and editorial choices are operator-only.
item.no_test_required: Documentation/research/planning row — automated tests not applicable
done_signal: Public URL recorded in success-plan.md and README.md; submission record archived under docs/content/building-gormes/strategy/writeups/.

item.name: Agentic-porting-kit extraction spec

item.degraded_mode: Without a written extraction boundary, a builder can copy Gormes-local process into a public repo that still depends on Gormes paths and cannot prove the methodology is portable.
ready_when: Phase 8 toolkit extraction is selected for planning.
The existing gormes-* skill list is known.
not_ready_when: The plan attempts to create the external repo before defining standalone acceptance.
The spec omits the non-Gormes example fixture or skill rename map.
acceptance: agentic-porting-kit.md names the public repo shape, README promise, license requirement, standalone example, and validation command.
The spec maps each gormes-* skill to a generic kit skill name.
success-plan.md links to the spec from the Q2 toolkit milestone.
The follow-on public repo scaffold row references the spec.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-13: wrote the agentic-porting-kit extraction spec before touching the external repo. item.name: Upstream Hermes user-stories static mirror
item.contract: The static Gormes docs mirror for upstream Hermes user stories must expose the current source-backed story count, category rollup, and fresh representative entries from `hermes-agent/website/src/data/userStories.json` instead of collapsing the page to an omitted interactive component. The mirror is intentionally a static summary, not a copied React grid or a duplicate quote database.
item.degraded_mode: Without the static summary, Gormes' upstream archive hides the community-proof surface that Hermes publishes publicly, so docs/public parity looks stale even when the upstream submodule is current.
ready_when: `./hermes-agent/website/src/data/userStories.json` is present in the refreshed upstream Hermes checkout.
`webpages/docs/content/upstream-hermes/user-stories.md` exists as the static mirror page.
The docs test can compare source JSON counts/categories to the static markdown without a live browser or network.
not_ready_when: The slice copies all 121 quote bodies into the mirror instead of publishing a compact summary.
The mirror depends on the upstream React component or client-side data loader at docs build time.
The row is used to add Gormes customer claims; this is an upstream-Hermes archive mirror only.
acceptance: TestUpstreamHermesUserStoriesStaticMirror fails while the mirror contains only `Upstream interactive component omitted from the static mirror` and passes after the page includes the source-derived total, top category rollup, and fresh entry headlines.
The static page states it summarizes `hermes-agent/website/src/data/userStories.json` from upstream Hermes and records the current 121-story count.
The page includes at least the top five source-derived category counts and representative fresh headlines from the e62250453 addition without duplicating every quote.
The upstream archive build still emits `/upstream-hermes/user-stories/` and markdown lint/content tests stay green.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-10: bounded all-topic weakness sweep covered CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public surfaces, and release/operator flows. Runtime/tooling deltas from current Hermes 3800972dd are complete or row-backed, including native `vision_analyze`; higher-priority P1 publication and release-parent rows remain operator-blocked or too broad. Fresh upstream public-surface evidence e62250453 expanded `website/src/data/userStories.json` from 99 to 117 entries, while the Gormes upstream mirror still rendered only an omitted-component placeholder. Planned rows were 19, below the 90-row cap, so adding this one source-backed P1 docs row was allowed. TDD added a docs test that compares the upstream JSON source to the static mirror, then replaced the placeholder with a compact source-derived summary: 117-story count, top category rollup, representative fresh entries, and an explicit boundary that these are upstream Hermes stories rather than Gormes customer claims. Green-repair refresh 2026-05-10: Hermes 3d4297a59 expanded the data file to 121 entries; the static mirror count and top `personal-assistant` category row were refreshed during the LINE plugin manifest pass so `go test ./webpages/docs -count=1` stays green against Hermes 7312f7f84.
done_signal: Static upstream-Hermes user-stories mirror shows the current source-backed count/category rollup and fresh entries; focused docs test plus full docs package pass.
